question: When was Khandesh merged into the Mughal empire by Akbar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1601**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1601, Mughal Emperor Akbar **incorporated **Khandesh **into the** Mughal empire.**
 
• Khandesh had been under the rule of the **Farooqi dynasty **since **1382**, established by **Malik Ahmad.**
 
• Akbar's conquest involved occupying Burhanpur in 1599 and besieging Asirgarh Fort, which he successfully took on January 17, 1601.
 
• Despite resistance from the ruler of the Khandesh Sultanate, Miran Bahadur Shah, Akbar appointed Prince Daniyal to oversee the newly established Subahs of Ahmadnagar, Berar, and Khandesh.
 
• Akbar had initiated administrative reforms in 1572, creating the first twelve subahs, which included Kabul, Lahore, Multan, Delhi, Agra, Avadh, Illahabad, Bihar, Bangal, Malwa, Ajmer, and Gujarat.
 
• Following his conquest of the Deccan, Akbar further expanded his administrative divisions, establishing three additional subahs: Berar, Khandesh, and Ahmadnagar.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Abu'l-Fath Jalal-ud-din Muhammad Akbar, **widely recognized as **Akbar the Great**, was the **third Mughal emperor**, reigning from **1556 to 1605.**
 
• Akbar ascended to the throne after his father, Humayun, and was initially supported by a regent,
 
• Bairam Khan, who aided in expanding and consolidating Mughal territories in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• Under Akbar's rule, Mughal India experienced significant economic growth, tripling in both size and wealth, which facilitated commercial expansion and fostered the flourishing of an Indo-Persian culture.
 
• Following Akbar's reign, his son, Prince Salim, later known as Jahangir, succeeded him as emperor.
